items.title: 通信部长蒂米尔西纳称：正在推进政策与法律改革以遏制社交媒体滥用
items.titleEn: Minister for Communication Dr. Timilsina says policy and legal reforms underway to curb social media misuse
items.status: DeepSeek 正文分析 · 待 Codex 核验
items.statusEn: DeepSeek article analysis · pending Codex review
items.summary: 据Technology Khabar报道，通信与信息技术部长维克拉姆·蒂米尔西纳在众议院会议上回答议员提问时表示，政府正在准备政策和法律改革，以应对社交媒体上的诈骗、诽谤和虚假信息传播。他提到《大众传播法案》和《新闻委员会法案》的起草准备工作正在进行，将很快提交议会。他还表示，通信部、内政部、尼泊尔警方网络局和尼泊尔电信管理局之间正在就网络诈骗管控进行协调，并称迄今为止已识别并关闭超过30.5万个博彩网站和新的博彩应用。
items.summaryEn: According to Technology Khabar, Minister for Communication and Information Technology Dr. Vikram Timilsina, responding to lawmakers' questions in a House of Representatives meeting, said the government is preparing policy and legal reforms to address fraud, defamation and dissemination of false and misleading information on social media. He stated that drafting of a Mass Communication Bill, a Press Council Bill and other legislation is underway, and that the bills will soon be presented to Parliament. He also said coordination is ongoing among the Ministry of Communication, Ministry of Home Affairs, Nepal Police Cyber Bureau and the Nepal Telecommunications Authority to control cyber fraud, and that more than 305,000 unique betting sites and new betting apps have so far been identified and shut down.
items.analysis: 条件性分析：若上述立法和协调机制按部长所述推进，则尼泊尔社交媒体平台、互联网服务提供商和网络用户可能面临更明确的平台责任与内容监管要求。对普通用户而言，短期影响可能体现在网络诈骗和虚假信息投诉渠道的进一步整合；对平台和ISP而言，则取决于法案具体条款是否引入新的合规或下架义务。下一步核查：应查阅众议院议事记录和通信部公开的《大众传播法案》《新闻委员会法案》草案文本，确认条款内容、提交时间及是否涉及平台义务。证据缺口：本条仅为部长在议会上的口头表态，未提供法案条款、生效时间表或具体执法数据来源；30.5万博彩网站数量的统计口径和核查方式也未说明，因此不应将其视为独立核实的事实。
items.analysisEn: Conditional analysis: if the legislative and coordination measures described by the minister proceed as stated, Nepali social media platforms, internet service providers and online users could face clearer platform responsibility and content-regulation requirements. For ordinary users, short-term impact may be seen mainly in further consolidation of reporting channels for online fraud and misinformation; for platforms and ISPs, it depends on whether the bills introduce new compliance or takedown obligations. Next verification step: review the House of Representatives records and the publicly released draft texts of the Mass Communication Bill and Press Council Bill to confirm provisions, submission timing and whether platform obligations are covered. Evidence gaps: this item rests on oral statements by the minister in Parliament, with no bill provisions, timeline or primary source for the enforcement figures; the methodology behind the 305,000 betting-site figure is not explained, so it should not be treated as independently verified fact.
